# Scraper API — Live Service

## Auth
All API requests require:
```
Authorization: Bearer <SCRAPE_API_KEY>
```
SCRAPE_API_KEY is set via `netlify env:set SCRAPE_API_KEY <key>`. Any shared secret works — NOT a Netlify PAT.

## Endpoints
- POST /api/scrape — Submit batch scrape (sync or queue)
- GET /api/status/{batchId} — Check batch status
- GET /api/result/{batchId}/{index} — Get result metadata + blob URL (NOT bytes)
- GET /api/result/{batchId}/{index}?passthrough=1 — Get raw bytes (costs bandwidth)
- GET /api/list — List recent batches
- POST /api/trigger-build — Creates deploy via API (does NOT trigger build plugin)
- POST /api/resume — Resume incomplete batches

## Queue processing limitation
API deploys do NOT trigger the build process. Only `netlify deploy` CLI or Git push runs the build plugin (which processes the queue). For automated queue processing, use GitHub Actions cron with `netlify deploy`.

## E2E flow
1. POST /api/scrape (queue=true) → batch_id
2. `netlify deploy` (CLI) or git push → processes queue
3. GET /api/status/{batchId} → poll until complete
4. GET /api/result/{batchId}/0 → blob_url (metadata, NOT bytes)
5. GET {blob_url} with NETLIFY_PAT → raw bytes (free, no bandwidth)

## Engines: fetch | chrome_impersonate | puppeteer
## TLS profiles: chrome120 (default) | firefox | safari | custom object
## Result modes: blob (default) | inline | metadata | auto
## Limits: 50 jobs sync, 500 queue, 5 concurrency sync, 10 queue

## Env vars on function:
- SCRAPE_API_KEY (optional — API auth)
- NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN + SITE_ID (for trigger-build — creates deploy, but build plugin requires CLI/Git)
